samples.marker_line: StormAttack loader: injection, hidden persistence and self-deletion
evidence: Entry 0x402674 reaches dispatch 0x401cb0. The configuration DWORD at VA 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401f75, Active Setup installation 0x401900, then cleanup 0x401390.

0x401900 creates an HKLM Active Setup component and writes REG_EXPAND_SZ StubPath at 0x401a4b. It reads its own file, changes configuration/resource bytes, writes another executable and launches the copy at 0x401b7e. Mode 4 calls 0x401b90 to extract and inject its DLL.

The alternate mode-1 path extracts resource 101 through 0x402460, writes the resource through 0x4023c0, deletes LanmanServer\Parameters\ServiceDLL and sets the replacement REG_EXPAND_SZ in 0x401260. Mode 2 installs an auto-start service; 0x402181 sets attributes 6 (Hidden|System). These are present capabilities, not a claim every branch ran in one execution.

0x401150 creates a target process, allocates remote memory, copies the DLL pathname with WriteProcessMemory, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA and starts it with CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. 0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del <own short path> > nul and launches it at 0x4014b8.

The embedded PE at 0x5060 has length 0x9c00 and entry RVA 0x741a containing zero bytes. Its code/import regions are largely zeroed. Storm banners identify the intended payload lineage, but do not establish an operational DDoS DLL, Remcos or ransomware.

Hidden self-installation, system service replacement, injection and shell cleanup tip the balance independently of the collector filename and sandbox score. No deployment authorization, runtime success or final working payload is supplied.

samples.marker_line: Apex2/NYX bot: remote floods and shell; add tasking and cron traits
evidence: Build information identifies apex2/Bot and module apex2, with linux/arm GOARM=7. Link flags embed server 176.65.139.201:443 and a bot token. The supplied Mirai feed label is broader than the recovered Apex2/NYX identity.

main.init.0 (0x28d628) configures logging, checks root, daemonizes and installs persistence unless NYX_NOPERSIST is set. main.main connects by net.DialTimeout, performs a handshake, registers, sends reconnaissance, starts encrypted pings and enters readLoop (0x28dbec). Root checks are not a privilege escalation exploit.

readLoop decrypts frames with protocol.Cipher.OpenFrame and dispatches attack, stop, update, execution and recon tasks. Opcode 0x3c creates a goroutine targeting main.handleExec through wrapper 0x28e05c. handleExec (0x2911bc) sends the received text to exec.CommandContext with /bin/sh -c, obtains CombinedOutput and returns it through SealFrame and WriteFrame.

Attack commands reach main.startAttack (0x28e228), parse duration, create a timeout context and call attack.StartFromLine. SourceEngine worker 0x24aba0 dials a UDP socket and repeatedly writes game query payloads until cancellation. L4 transport/amplification and L7 rapid-reset/flood implementations are compiled into the dispatcher. A plaintext Source Engine payload is present; encoding is not required.

persist.installLinux (0x25e980) writes system and user systemd units, /etc/cron.d root @reboot entries, rc.local/init.d scripts, user crontab, .bashrc and XDG autostart entries. These are concrete startup mechanisms, not merely service-related strings.

handleUpdate (0x28f4d0) downloads bytes, writes a replacement beside the current executable, chmods, renames and starts the replacement. This is a remotely requested self-update capability; runtime completion was not observed.

Recon.Collect (0x28cb18) builds a report from host/user/workdir, network interfaces/default route, SSH key filenames, AWS profile names, browser store existence and cloud metadata. Browsers uses os.Stat, not secret reads. AWS reads ~/.aws/credentials but selects bracketed profile names, not access-key values; SSHKeys lists .ssh names. Do not turn this into unsupported credential-content theft.

Handshake.ClientFin calls util.SharedSecret (X25519) and DeriveKeyFixed (HKDF), then authenticates handshake material with HMAC. These are reachable protocol operations; new notable API references describe the corresponding implementations.

The fixed bot enrollment, remote flooding, arbitrary shell execution, reconnaissance return and automatic startup distinguish this configured implant from ordinary load-testing tools. The operator and installation history are unknown; no bot traffic was executed for this review.

samples.identification: UniClipboard 1.5.0-alpha.2 source archive and dual-side-sync development skill
samples.marker_line: UniClipboard source: registry badges and SSH sync; fix C2/AMOS FPs
evidence: Inspected tar contents, Cargo workspace/build declarations, README, daemon engine event forwarding, clipboard platform code, package-status workflow and script, and the dual-side-sync script. The requested .claude/skills/dual-side-sync path is absent in these bytes; the actual skill is under .agents/skills/dual-side-sync.

package-status.py fetches package registry metadata. winget_version reads directory entries from the GitHub Contents API and sorts their names as versions. aur_version runs a fixed argv git clone of the AUR package repository and parses .SRCINFO. No remotely supplied value becomes a command.
collect uses a ThreadPoolExecutor, writes SVG badges and local status.json, and prints the snapshot. The hostile rule joined these independent capabilities into a nonexistent command channel.

The sync script requires operator-provided host/user/repository configuration. push computes tracked/untracked working-set paths, uses rsync over SSH and explicitly deletes the locally deleted paths on the remote checkout. reset and arbitrary ssh commands are explicitly selected CLI operations. install-rsync fetches a named rsync distribution and updates the remote user PATH.

The skill documentation claims HEAD/clean-tree gating, but the current push implementation explicitly omits those checks. This documentation drift is not evidence of secret theft or a concealed command channel. SSH transfer, execution and deletion remain real dual-use capabilities.
The AMOS hit comes from an ordinary /p2p path in an architecture document. That path supplies neither family identity nor exfiltration. The path observation remains notable at its neutral home.

The separately fetched versionless dependency has archive SHA bca070c7dd9f1f5e6c3af195a5b755072d01f2f98e81ba769a12822a3850c113 in both isolation scans. Its package-status.py and p2p document hashes equal the corresponding supplied-archive members. Corrections apply to shared rules, without dependent-package exceptions.

The inspected actions fit clipboard synchronization and project maintenance. No hidden hostile source-to-effect chain is established. The compiled application, omitted deployment history and external engine dependency are not certified by this source-archive judgment.

verification.store_near_miss: Ordinary C++ pathname constant fires at suspicious before and notable after; copied outside testdata to avoid the existing test-path exclusion.
verification.worker_near_miss: Compiled benign linux/arm Go program defines a noinline startAttack that only prints a local game-action message. Before: suspicious objective. After: notable metadata, zero hostile/suspicious findings.
verification.native_mutations: Removing the command-received format or both result-error formats from original ARM bytes removes only the new encrypted command and dependent cron hostile findings. Removing @reboot root removes only the new cron hostile finding. Original three hostile findings remain in every control.
verification.forager: Recovered SHA efe9080720de136ceb5165edd0bd6ffe6003cf25024ed29363e0959ed15922d7 (C# GitHub backdoor) and SHA 88a6e45dd2c51af5d67faefda91a8f7df0175aa1b3cb7979d210fcc68d39ac7a (AMD64 NYX bot) through Hopper/forager; original bytes and .forage.json remain in scratch.

remaining_disagreements: The supplied benign UniClipboard archive remains ML-flagged with probability 1.0 and level 0 despite zero hostile/suspicious findings across its members and fetched dependencies. This is a remaining classifier false positive, not grounds to restore inaccurate traits.

The isolated GitHub dependency has zero hostile/suspicious findings and remains below the calibrated ML alert grid (level -1). Its raw probability is recorded separately; the rule correction must not be judged from that number alone.
Atomscan reports feature schema v18 versus expected v21; recent traits may be absent from this model. Raw detection coverage is verified independently of the ensemble.

The Windows percent-decoded fact comes from a GUID printf format, not a concealed executable URL. The inert embedded DLL prevents claims of a working final-stage DDoS payload; outer loader behavior independently supports MALICIOUS.
external_sources: The supplied Triage, Bazaar and GitHub URLs could not be retrieved with the web tool. Their scores/family/manifest labels were not used as behavioral proof.
